item.text:
**Bottom Line**
3B.1 is **mostly negative / mixed with limited corrective action**. The 2024 record is dominated by credible reporting of ongoing abuse in Papua, weak investigation, and continued political arrests. The clearest pro-protection evidence is a **reactive army apology and detention of 13 soldiers** after a torture video, not a demonstrated system-wide restraint.

**Accepted Claims**
- **“If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?”: Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-09-18** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in) | HRW says Indonesian security forces committed arbitrary arrests and detention, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass forced displacement in Papua, and were seldom held to account. This is strong evidence **against** Jokowi’s government adequately protecting residents from state violence. | **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **UN Human Rights Committee findings on Indonesia** | **OHCHR / UN Geneva Multimedia Newsroom** | **2024-03-28** | [URL](https://www.unognewsroom.org/teleprompter/en/2120/ohchr-press-conference-un-human-rights-committees-findings-28-march-2024/6411) | The Committee said it was concerned by multiple reports of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances of indigenous people in Papua that had not been investigated. This directly supports a **negative** finding on protection and accountability. | **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Human Rights Reports: Indonesia** | **U.S. Department of State** | **published 2025-08-12; report covers 2024** | [URL](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | The report says violence between government forces and separatists continued in Papua, with credible reports of arbitrary killings, torture, and excessive force by security officials, and that the government did not systematically take credible steps to identify and punish abusive officials. This is the strongest broad negative evidence. | **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Indonesian Army apologizes after torture video goes viral** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-03-28** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/28/indonesian-army-apologizes-after-torture-video-goes-viral) | The army apologized after a torture video from Papua and detained 13 soldiers for inquiry. This is the clearest **partial positive** signal, but it is reactive and does not show systematic protection or durable accountability. | **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Annual Overview 2024** | **Papuans Behind Bars** | **2025-07-23; covers 2024** | [URL](https://papuansbehindbars.org/annual-overview-2024/) | The overview recorded 370 political arrests in 2024, with most detainees released within hours or days and only a small fraction prosecuted. This cuts both ways: it shows continued arbitrary political arrests, but also that prolonged imprisonment was not universal. | **3B.1**, **2B.9**

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Jokowi’s government implemented a broad, successful nationwide program to reduce state violence, torture, disappearances, or arbitrary punishment.
- The available evidence is heavily concentrated in **Papua**, where the record is mostly adverse.
- The best positive evidence is **case-specific and reactive** rather than proof of sustained protection.
